newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end easier, shrug off industrial output data.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end easier, shrug off industrial output data.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond futures contract ended easier on Thursday, pushed down by position-adjustment sales that appeared toward the close.

"Day traders who bought the March at around the intraday low of 126.18 in the morning probably liquidated their positions toward the close," a trader for a long-term credit bank's securities unit said.
The March ended at 126.28, down slightly from the previous day's close of 126.36, after moving in a range between 126.18 to 126.44 during the day.
Traders said industrial output data, which was released in the afternoon, sent mixed signals to the market.

Although industrial output in January came out strong, some traders bought JGBs based on the weak forecasts for output in February and March, the trader for a long-term credit bank's securities unit said.
The impact from the data was limited, however, because the government did not alter its view on production trends, a trader for an agricultural financial institution said.
The Ministry of International Trade and Industry said in a statement that industrial output was on an upward trend.
The Ministry of International Trade and Industry said Japan's industrial production in January increased a preliminary 5.3 percent from the previous month.
MITI also said manufacturers' output is seen down 3.3 percent month-on-month in February and down 2.7 percent month-on-month in March.
Earlier, JGBs ended the morning session slightly down following an overnight plunge in U.S. Treasuries.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond closed sharply lower on Wednesday in reaction to Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before the Senate Banking Committee.
Greenspan said the Fed may need to raise interest rates before actual evidence of real inflation emerges.
But the impact of Greenspan's comments on the JGB market was limited, as his comments had little overall effect on Tokyo share prices, traders said.
In the Tokyo stock market, the 225-share Nikkei average finished 30.64 points, or 0.16 percent, higher at 19,021.56.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.385 percent as of 0708 GMT, up from the previous day's close of 2.400 percent.
